title: Session-anchored shadow pressure canary with auto-quarantine and rollback advisor
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- New rollout mode: session-anchored shadow pressure canary.
- Auto-quarantine: cohorts showing drift are isolated automatically.
- Rollback advisor: automated recommendations + safe revert playbook.
- Backwards-compatible config; opt-in via rollout.strategy.type="session-shadow-pressure".
commits: feat: add session-anchoring primitives to scheduler (session_anchor.go)
feat: implement pressure simulator and quota-aware shadowing (pressure_simulator.go)
feat: quarantine manager and automated isolation policy (quarantine_manager.go)
feat: rollout rollback advisor with drift scoring and counterfactual checks (rollback_advisor.go)
docs: runbook and example configs for new rollout mode
test: integration/e2e scenarios and smoke tests
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see regressions that only appear when model behavior is exercised under realistic session patterns (long-lived sessions, stateful KV cache reuse). Existing canaries and shadow modes don't replicate session composition or allow controlled load pressure against shadow variants. This PR introduces a new rollout strategy ('session-shadow-pressure') that combines session-consistent shadowing with adjustable pressure testing and an automated quarantine/rollback advisor pipeline.

Design summary: The mode has three coordinated pieces: (1) Session anchoring in the router/scheduler so the same user-session is consistently routed to the same canary/shadow instance for the duration of the window; (2) Pressure simulator that can replay production traffic shapes (qps, token distribution, concurrency) against shadow replicas at configurable fractions and can override sampling to stress KV-cache hit/miss scenarios; (3) Quarantine manager + rollback advisor that monitors multi-dimensional drift signals (semantic regressions, latency tail, token costs, hallucination heuristics) and either triggers cohort quarantine or surfaces an automated rollback recommendation with suggested revert commit + playbook.

Config knobs and API: New rollout.strategy.type = "session-shadow-pressure". Key parameters (all optional): session_ttl_seconds, pressure_fraction, pressure_profile (burst|steady|spike), kv_cache_stress (low|med|high), drift_thresholds (json-encoded metric thresholds), quarantine_window_seconds, rollback_advisor_enabled (bool). The openapi doc and example YAML are included.

Runtime changes: session_anchor.go augments the request router to stamp and persist a session token (cookie/header) and attach session affinity metadata to a serving token so in-flight requests reuse the same cache lane and physical pod selection. The pressure_simulator hooks into the routing layer and the traffic mirror pipeline to apply controlled amplification factors and synthetic cache churn. quarantine_manager.go implements an actor that marks cohorts as "quarantined" and transitions their traffic to a safe baseline variant while preserving telemetry for postmortem. rollback_advisor.go computes a drift score using weighted signals and attempts quick counterfactuals (replay the cohort against the previous model snapshot) to validate rollback recommendations.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests for session affinity edge cases, integration tests that run a 30-minute pressure profile against a small cluster in CI, and two e2e scenarios that assert quarantine and rollback advisor behavior under injected semantic drift. The PR includes a lightweight local simulator (examples/session-shadow-pressure.yaml) so SRE and SE can reproduce locally.

Operational considerations: Default behavior is opt-in and conservative (pressure_fraction defaults to 0.01; quarantine requires sustained drift > threshold for quarantine_window_seconds). Rollback advisor issues a non-destructive recommendation by default (no automatic rollback unless rollback_advisor_enabled=true and rollout.auto_revert=true). Audit logs are emitted for quarantine/rollback actions and exposed in the console.

Migration and compatibility: No changes required for existing rollout configs. New fields are ignored by older controllers. For Dedicated/Private deployments, the pressure simulator toggles are gated behind operator flags to avoid unintended load on customer hardware.

Checklists: - [x] API + OpenAPI changes documented and example config added. - [x] Scheduler/session affinity implemented and covered by unit tests. - [x] Pressure simulator and config referenced in runbook. - [x] Quarantine manager emits alerts and writes audit events. - [x] Rollback advisor runs counterfactual replays in a sandbox and provides deterministic recommendations. - [x] Manual QA run in staging with full traffic replay completed.

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam O'Connor (review): "This looks solid overall. Two requests: add rate-limits to the pressure_simulator to avoid overload in small clusters, and ensure TTLs are bounded to prevent session token proliferation."
- Maya (author): "Added rate-limiter and bounded TTL (configurable with safe defaults). See scheduler changes commit and unit tests."
- Diego Martinez (review): "Can we add an opt-out for KV cache stress in Dedicated clusters? Also add an alert routing note for SRE on quarantine events."
- Maya: "Added operator gate and alert routing doc. CI e2e passes locally and in the shared staging project."
- Sana Iyer (approval): "Verified e2e scenario reproduces expected quarantine + recommended rollback. Approving with one minor doc ask; added inline."

CI summary: Initial pipeline failed on flakey integration test (timeout under 30s), re-run after increasing timeouts; all checks pass (unit, lint, integration, e2e smoke). Performance microbenchmarks show median latency impact <1% at pressure_fraction=0.01 and acceptable tail increases at higher stress levels noted in docs.

Merge decision and post-merge steps: Squashed and merged to main. Post-merge: (1) ops to enable example flags in staging (infra PR: infra/k8s/rollout-crd.yaml), (2) schedule a 1-hour staged canary in staging and one small canary in dedicated testing clusters, (3) run the provided smoke playbook in docs/runbooks/session-shadow-pressure.md.

Related work and references: ENG-4127 (design spike for session-consistent shadowing), ENG-4132 (rollback advisor prototype), runbook and example configs included.

Caveats and known limitations: The counterfactual replayer expects determinism; non-deterministic models (sampling hot seeds) may produce noisy drift scores. We added heuristics and confidence bounds but recommend human review on ambiguous advisories.

If anything is unclear or you'd like a short walkthrough, I can demo the staging runbook and the console quarantine trace.
